glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: bug
  Severity: high
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_core.py — `_flag_tags` (new `if item.get("reason") == _UNBOUND_COVERS:` block)
  Finding: The unbound-covers branch is inserted *after* the pre-existing filter `if not isinstance(item, dict) or not _is_test_id(str(item.get("test") or "")): continue`. Unbound items are constructed in `_suite_tags._unbound` with `test=""`. If `_is_test_id("")` is False (very likely — it checks a `file::test` id against `_TEST_DIRS`), every unbound item is dropped by that first `continue` and the new warning branch is dead code. Similarly, the warning's own guard `_is_test_id(str(item.get("raw") or "").split(":", 1)[0])` passes a bare file path with no `::` into a helper that validates test ids — if that returns False, the warning is silently swallowed. The new tests in `shared/tests/test_tag_binding_unbound_covers.py` assert the warning *is* emitted, so either these pass (and the helpers are lenient in a way worth confirming), or the gate never warns and the spec's "routes it to warnings" is not met. Verify `_is_test_id` behavior for `""` and for a path-only prefix; if either returns False, hoist the unbound check above the `_is_test_id(test)` filter and drop/replace the `_is_test_id(raw-prefix)` guard (e.g. check the path is a test file instead).
  Suggestion: Move the `reason == _UNBOUND_COVERS` dispatch to the top of the loop body, before the generic `continue` filters, and validate the file path with the same predicate used to decide which files the collector runs on.

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/_suite_tags.py — `pending_at`
  Finding: `pending_at` is only assigned in the `elif same_line_covers is not None:` branch (and the two-consecutive-covers sub-branch). The primary covers-comment path (the `cm` branch handling a line that is only a `// @covers`, not shown in the diff and therefore unchanged) sets `pending` without setting `pending_at`, since that branch predates the variable. Any unbound comment flowing through that branch is reported with a stale `pending_at` (initially 0, so raw reads `path:0: // @covers …`). The new tests never assert the reported line number, so this would pass CI while emitting wrong line numbers in warnings and audit output.
  Suggestion: Set `pending_at = lineno` wherever `pending` is first assigned (including the covers-comment-only branch), and add a test asserting the raw contains the actual line number (e.g. `a.test.ts:1:` for the import case, `:2:` for the blank-line case).

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/test_suite_tags_lexer.py — `test_covers_above_an_import_is_reported_once_and_never_rebound`, `test_covers_separated_from_describe_by_a_blank_line_is_reported`, `test_two_consecutive_covers_lines_report_the_overwritten_first_one`
  Finding: These tests assert only `reason` and that the FR id appears somewhere in `raw`; they never check the line number or that exactly one report is produced per dropped comment in the two-consecutive case beyond a `len == 1`. Combined with the `pending_at` issue above, an implementation reporting `path:0:` or a wrong line would still pass. Also, the raw format string is asserted nowhere, so downstream consumers (`_flag_tags` splits `raw` on `":"` taking element 0 as a path) are untested against the actual producer format — the shared-side test hand-writes a raw string rather than round-tripping the collector's output.
  Suggestion: Assert the full raw (or at least `f"{PATH}:{lineno}:"` prefix), and add one round-trip test that feeds `propagate_suite_tags` output into `evaluate` so the producer/consumer raw format contract is enforced.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/_tag_binding_core.py — `_is_test_id(str(item.get("raw") or "").split(":", 1)[0])`
  Finding: On a Windows/absolute path (`C:\repo\tests\a.test.ts`), `split(":", 1)[0]` yields `C`, so a legitimate unbound covers warning would be dropped. Low-impact if the guard is removed per the high finding above.
  Suggestion: Remove the guard or parse the path up to the `: // @covers` marker instead.

- Category: spec
  Severity: low
  File: (diff-wide)
  Finding: The spec calls for regenerating `test-traceability.json` once as the last step and listing moved FRs in the PR. No traceability regeneration is visible in the diff (may be intentionally out-of-diff, but it is an acceptance item). Confirm it was done; otherwise the moved/renamed FR coverage entries for the new test files will be stale.
  Suggestion: Run the traceability regeneration and include the artifact change in the PR.

The lexer-based depth counting itself (`_brace_deltas` with the joined source and per-line bisect) is sound — offsets are internally consistent even for `\r\n`/unicode line separators — and the `check_orphan` routing (excluded from fail conditions, worded apart) matches the spec, with tests covering the only-unbound and mixed cases.

Overall: the approach is right and the collector/audit side looks solid, but the gate-side routing in `_tag_binding_core` depends on unverified `_is_test_id` behavior that could make the warning path dead code, and the line-number reporting is likely wrong for the common covers-comment path — fix and add the corresponding assertions before merging.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
